experiments.study_type: Whole-body plethysmography during hypoxic-hypercapnic gas challenge (Study 1, vehicle cohort)
experiments.procedure_text: Rats received an intravenous vehicle injection, followed 15 min later by a 60 min HH gas challenge with whole-body plethysmography.
experiments.procedure_text_evidence: After 15 min, both groups received a HH gas challenge for 60 min before restoring the flow of room air.
experiments.test_system_evidence: was used to record ventilatory parameters in freely-moving rats
experiments.route_evidence: received an injection of vehicle (100 μL/kg, IV)

experiments.exposure_evidence: received an injection of vehicle (100 μL/kg, IV)
experiments.regulatory_evidence: according to the NIH Guide for Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (NIH Publication No. 80-23)
experiments.notes: The 326 ± 2 g cohort was run in two batches of 3, with 60 min of chamber acclimation and 30 min of recording after room air was restored. Table 5 lists time to return to pre-HH levels but the excerpt does not identify its cohorts.

experiments.study_type: Rectal body temperature recording during hypoxic-hypercapnic gas challenge (saline cohort)
experiments.procedure_text: Rat body temperature was recorded by rectal thermometer before and after saline injection, during a 60-min HH gas challenge, and after return to room air.
experiments.procedure_text_evidence: We also recorded rat body temperature at various timepoints during a 60-min HH gaschallenge
experiments.test_system_evidence: a thermistor probe was inserted 5-6 cm into the rectum
experiments.route_evidence: following the injection of vehicle (saline; n = 6 rats, 328 ± 3 g)

endpoints.label: Body temperature
endpoints.evidence: We recorded rat body temperatures before (Pre-drug) and at various timepoints (Post-drug)

substances.evidence: in 0.1 M, pH 7.4 phosphate-buffered saline

experiments.exposure_evidence: during a 60-min HH gaschallenge, and upon return to room-air
experiments.regulatory_evidence: according to the NIH Guide for Care and Use of Laboratory Animals (NIH Publication No. 80-23)
